item.title: Touring can take musicians to isolating, anxious extremes. Access to therapy on the road is a vital support
item.description: I know from our early days how high-pressure road life can be. While big tours often hire therapists, grassroots acts can’t afford it. I’m pleased to back a new scheme that aims to change that When Radiohead started touring, it was hugely exciting, but we got signed when we had been going for five or six years and had only really played in Oxford. Suddenly you’re entering a new world: the first flush of fame, being compared to everyone else, the furnace-like experience when a band takes off and a whole new routine of late nights, bad food and everything else that goes on around live music… Fuente: The Guardian - Culture.

item.title: ‘I never pass up a rewatch’: why Valley Girl is my feelgood movie
item.description: The latest in our series of writers explaining their most rewatched comfort films brings us back to 1980s LA As a teenager growing up in the 1990s, I was deeply obsessed with all things 1980s pop culture. Chalk it up to nostalgia for my Care Bears-filled childhood – or a stubborn adolescent desire to separate myself from the Dave Matthews Band-loving, khaki-wearing kids at my high school. (Mission accomplished: it’s safe to say I was the only person I knew rocking a bandana tied around my pants leg or a Wild Boys-era Duran Duran shirt.) Back then, I was especially drawn to 1980s teen movies… Fuente: The Guardian - Culture.

item.title: ‘Pretenders’ Review: A Superb Portrait of Chrissie Hynde and Her Legendary Band Captures Their Incandescence…and Tragedy
item.description: Hynde, though she had the feelings of punk in her bones, was the most romantic songwriter of that entire scene. item.title: Prima Facie review – fiery one-woman play is flattened into a bland movie
item.description: Toronto film festival: Cynthia Erivo takes on the role Jodie Comer made famous for a pointless adaptation of a story about rape and retribution that loses the power it once had Suzie Miller’s award-winning 2019 play Prima Facie employs a familiar narrative device: a hotshot London barrister finds herself on the other side of the bar, subject to the very legal tactics she once so ruthlessly employed. Not as a defendant, but as the accuser in a rape case. item.description: Call Me Maybe made the singer-songwriter famous – but also confused. Who was she? Who was her music for? item.title: 'Spiderman', 'Friends' o 'Lilo & Stitch': el desconocido impacto del 11-S en la cultura pop
item.description: Veinticinco años después, el cine, la televisión, la música y la literatura se convirtieron en el reflejo del trauma de Estados Unidos. En esta crónica especial analizamos los efectos que tuvieron los mortíferos atentados del 11 de septiembre 2001 sobre la cultura popular estadounidense, y cómo todas estas obras nos permiten hoy en día entender la complejidad del mundo que nació tras estos ataques terroristas. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
